description: JSON parameter wire form: the generated JSON type is written by exec, a batch of lone placeholders, copyfrom and a batch of rows and read back, and the stored document is described with the engine's own functions, compared with the same text as a literal and found by the document as a parameter; the document holds spacing, key order, a trailing zero, HTML characters and two- and four-byte UTF-8. ClickHouse's JSON type normalises a document. The native emitter writes the document as text. Reads: the native driver reads a JSON column only into a chcol.JSON, a chcol.JSONDeserializer, a struct or a map, so generated reads go through the converting scan adapter, a chcol.JSONDeserializer, in a one-row read, a stream, a UNION ALL whose second arm has a parameter of its own, an embed and a runtime builder, a Nullable(JSON) column (NULL and a document), and inside Array(JSON), Array(Nullable(JSON)), Map(String, JSON) (scanned entry by entry), Map(String, Nullable(JSON)), Map(String, Array(JSON)), a Map of named tuples, a named Tuple, an unnamed Tuple, and an Array and a Map of unnamed tuples. Every document reads as the text json.Marshal writes for clickhouse-go's chcol.JSON, the same bytes as case 122 reads through database/sql; a richer document shows the spelling: keys sorted, HTML characters escaped, a date path as a Go time, a 64-bit integer unquoted, 1e21 as 1e+21, null and empty-object paths dropped, against toJSONString's own text.
